identified_problem: AustralianSuper is Australia’s largest superannuation fund, managing over $430 billion in retirement savings on behalf of more than 3.6 million members. The 2019–20 Black Summer bushfires and the 2022 NSW/Queensland floods caused tens of billions of dollars in damage across Australian property, infrastructure and agriculture, directly affecting the long-dated assets in AustralianSuper’s portfolio.
climate_exposure: Its domestic and global property, infrastructure and equity holdings are exposed to physical climate risks including wildfire, inland flood and heat stress.
potential_pain: Concentrated losses in fire- or flood-prime regions can drag on fund-level returns, increase portfolio volatility and complicate member retirement outcomes without granular hazard intelligence.
evidence: Address-level wildfire and flood exposure layers plus historical event intelligence for the 2019–20 Black Summer and 2022 eastern-Australia floods, mapped to AustralianSuper’s Australian asset footprint.
recommended_message: Show AustralianSuper how Talaix hazard layers can quantify physical climate risk across its property and infrastructure allocations, using the same wildfire and flood events already reshaping Australian asset values.
fit_score: As the country’s largest superannuation fund with long-duration infrastructure and property holdings, AustralianSuper has both the scale and the asset-class exposure to benefit from enterprise-grade physical climate analytics.

interactions.summary: Identified via official-source research; signal: AustralianSuper’s public profile states it is Australia’s largest super fund managing over $430 billion for more than 3.6 million members.
